title: Akshay Kumar Laughs Off Pan Masala Question as Bollywood's Endorsement Debate Returns
excerpt: A journalist's quip that 'everyone is selling kesar' drew a viral laugh from the actor, reviving scrutiny of Bollywood's pan masala endorsements just days after Maharashtra's FDA issued notices to Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn, and Tiger Shroff over surrogate advertising.
body:
• A journalist's remark that "sab kesar bech rahe hain" (everyone is selling kesar/saffron) at a press event drew a burst of laughter from Akshay Kumar, and the clip has gone viral on social media.
  • The moment arrives days after Maharashtra's FDA issued notices to Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn, and Tiger Shroff, demanding they stop appearing in surrogate advertisements for pan masala brand Vimal.
  • Akshay Kumar has his own complicated history with pan masala endorsements — he apologised in 2022 for endorsing Vimal Elaichi and donated the endorsement fee, but ads shot in 2021 continued airing until late 2023.
  • India's pan masala market is estimated at $5 billion, and health experts say the product is a leading cause of oral fibrosis that often progresses to oral cancer.

The Viral Moment

At a recent press event, a journalist's pointed observation about Bollywood's relationship with pan masala brands produced what has become one of the week's most-shared clips. The reporter remarked "sab kesar bech rahe hain" — a wry reference to the fact that multiple A-list actors endorse brands selling kesar (saffron) and elaichi (cardamom) products that serve as surrogates for banned pan masala. Akshay Kumar burst out laughing at the comment, and the video quickly went viral across social media platforms, The Times of India reported.

The moment resonated because it captured an awkward truth that Bollywood has struggled to address: some of the industry's biggest names continue to appear in advertisements for products widely understood to be proxies for tobacco-laced betel nut mixes.

The Surrogate Advertising Machine

Surrogate advertising is a marketing method in which companies promote a legal proxy product — club soda, cardamom, or saffron — using the same brand name, logo, and visual style as a prohibited product, keeping the main brand visible to consumers. In one Vimal cardamom advertisement, three actors appear in a festive celebration throwing saffron on one another. The ad has garnered 106 million views on YouTube.

On August 17, Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration issued notices to Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn, and Tiger Shroff, ordering them to stop appearing in Vimal's surrogate advertisements, Reuters reported. The FDA said the ads "appear to promote the VIMAL brand, which is mainly associated with pan masala," a prohibited betel nut product sold in tiny 3.5-rupee packs.

"Such use of the brand name and identity may have the effect of promoting, reinforcing or maintaining consumer recognition of the prohibited product."

— Maharashtra FDA notice to Bollywood actors

The Maharashtra authorities demanded the actors remove the advertisements from their social media accounts, halt any further broadcast cooperation, and provide details of their endorsement agreements with the manufacturer. Representatives of the actors and Vimal's parent company, Vishnu & Company Trademarks, did not respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

Akshay Kumar's Complicated History

Kumar has arguably the most complicated relationship with pan masala endorsements among Bollywood's top stars. He first endorsed Vimal Pan Masala in 2021, appearing alongside Shah Rukh Khan and Ajay Devgn. After swift backlash from fans who dug up an old video of the actor vowing never to promote tobacco, Kumar issued a public apology in April 2022.

"I am sorry. I would like to apologise to you, all my fans and well-wishers," he wrote. "While I have not and will not endorse tobacco, I respect the outpouring of your feelings. With all humility, I step back. I have decided to contribute the entire endorsement fee towards a worthy cause."

The story did not end there. In October 2023, when a new Vimal commercial aired during the ICC World Cup, Kumar faced renewed backlash. He responded sharply on X, clarifying that the ads had been shot on October 13, 2021, before his public disassociation. "They can legally run the already shot ads till the end of next month. Chill and do some real news," he told a media outlet.

At a Jolly LLB 3 trailer launch in Kanpur in 2025, when a journalist brought up the city's association with gutka, Kumar was unequivocal: "Gutka nahi khana chahiye. That's it. Next question."

A $5 Billion Industry Under Pressure

India's pan masala market was worth an estimated $5 billion last year, according to industry estimates cited by Reuters. Health experts and doctors have identified it as a leading cause of oral fibrosis that often progresses to oral cancer. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government has previously expressed concern about surrogate advertisements, and India was drafting stricter rules in 2024 to bar the practice after complaints that liquor companies were also using brand-name proxies, though those rules remain unfinalized.

The Maharashtra FDA's enforcement drive has added a new dimension to the debate. Under Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, the agency has shut restaurants, suspended quick-commerce warehouse permits, and now turned its attention to the celebrity endorsement ecosystem that keeps pan masala brands culturally visible.

Where the Industry Goes From Here

Not all actors have followed the endorsement path. Sunny Deol stated publicly on August 17 that he would never do pan masala ads, saying he does not want to promote something he does not believe in. Anil Kapoor reportedly rejected a Rs 10 crore endorsement deal from a pan masala brand, citing his responsibility to audiences. Amitabh Bachchan terminated his Kamla Pasand contract in 2021 and later issued a legal notice demanding the brand stop airing commercials featuring him.

For now, Kumar's laughing reaction has done what the FDA notices, consumer court cases, and years of social media criticism have not — turned the absurdity of Bollywood's pan masala moment into a single, shareable clip that requires no commentary.
